analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: 2018 redux? Not so fast
key_insights: BofA argues there is always a Fed put for equities, but the strike depends on how large the inflation problem is.
The Fed will be less willing to support stocks than in 2019 and less unwilling than in 2022, because inflation is a problem now but a smaller one than in 2022.
Some analysts compare the current setup to 2018, when Fed hikes were priced out as equities sold off. The Fed hiked for the last time in Dec 2018 and began cutting the following summer.
The 2022 analogy is the alternative: the Fed hiked aggressively into an equity bear market and did not cut until late 2024.
BofA did not think last week's selloff was large enough to trigger the Fed put. After yesterday's rally, conviction rose that a December hike is nearly a lock.
BofA base case is additional hikes in January and March 2027, and it still expects 3 more hikes in total.
Fed pricing for cumulative hikes by March and June 2027 has nearly returned to levels seen after Gov. Waller's '50bp hike' speech and Oct CPI.
BofA 4Q GDP tracking is unchanged at 2.4% q/q saar after Oct housing starts, versus the official forecast of 2.3%.
Today's calendar: Sep Case-Shiller, FHFA HPI and Nov consumer confidence (BofA est 92.0, consensus 92.2).

macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA expects the hiking cycle to continue despite the equity selloff, so a Fed put is unlikely to be triggered soon.

risk_factors: A larger equity selloff than last week's could trigger a Fed put and short-circuit the hiking cycle.
An AI trade unwind could lead markets to price out Fed hikes, as in 2018.
Persistent inflation could keep the Fed less sensitive to equities, as in 2022.

tension_points.bull_case: Analysts who point to 2018 argue the equity selloff will price out Fed hikes and the Fed will support stocks.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA argues the Fed has an inflation problem now, so the put is struck lower than in 2018 and a December hike is nearly a lock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A larger equity selloff than last week's, big enough to trigger the Fed put, would invalidate the BofA hiking path.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed put exists but is struck lower than in 2018 because inflation is a problem, so hikes continue.
theme_stances.evidence: there's always a Fed put, but where it's struck depends on the data
